title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays in O(log(min(n, m)))
excerpt: Binary searching a partition instead of a value: how to find the median of two sorted arrays without merging them, and why the sentinels remove every edge case.
seoTitle: Median of Two Sorted Arrays — O(log(min(n,m))) Explained
seoDescription: A walkthrough of the logarithmic median-of-two-sorted-arrays algorithm: partitioning instead of merging, why only one cut is free to move, and why infinities beat special cases.

content.text: Two sorted arrays, one median. Merging them and indexing the middle is O(n + m) and takes about four lines. This page is about the O(log(min(n, m))) solution, which is the reason the problem is rated the way it is.
The interesting part is not the binary search itself. It is what you binary search
: not a value, but a place to cut.

Cut both arrays so the two left parts together hold exactly half the elements and every left value is <= every right value. Choosing the cut in one array forces the cut in the other, so there is only one unknown and it can be binary searched. Search the shorter array so the forced cut always lands in range, and treat the positions past each end as ∓∞ so empty arrays and one-sided cuts need no special handling.
Forget merging. A median is defined by a property: it sits at the point where half the combined elements are below and half above. So instead of producing the merged array, produce the

items.text: Not swapping so the shorter array is searched. j then goes out of bounds, usually on lopsided inputs like a length-1 array against a length-10 one.
Using < instead of <= in the cross conditions. With many equal values several cuts are valid; a strict comparison rejects them all and the search runs off the end.
Searching over [0, n-1] instead of [0, n]. Cutting after every element of a is a legal partition and is exactly what an empty or entirely-smaller a requires.
Special-casing empty arrays by hand instead of using sentinels. It works, but it is four branches that the infinities give you for free.
Returning an integer. With an even total the median can be a half-integer, so the return type has to be floating point.
